executiveSummary: GM1771 is identity-correct, deterministic and numerically complete for all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services, but it is not locally calibrated enough for release as an operational Geldrop-Mierlo first-72-hour forecast. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset produces a persistent precise local water/service trajectory without a selected hydraulically connected event, and eight unrelated hazards reuse exactly the same complete fifteen-neighbourhood order. That order conflicts with official municipal rain and heat evidence: Neerakkers is last despite a named Neerakker water project, while green Buitengebied Mierlo is ranked hottest although the municipality identifies the green zone between both cores as cooler. Official public pluvial scenarios, water-control registers, road/rail, provider territories, antennas, schools and acute-care records are valuable context, but do not establish live topology, capacity, passability, backups, acceptance or restoration. Desktop and mobile UI checks are mechanically accessible and disclose several source limitations, yet still put exact 69% drinking-water availability beside an unsupported local major-river event without an adjacent municipal support warning.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1771 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG places and BRT settlements
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS table identifies GM1771 as Geldrop-Mierlo and reports 40,754 residents, density 1,314 per square kilometre, 23.9% aged 65 or older and 6,414 one-person households. Published small-area fields may be rounded, suppressed, unavailable or not applicable; null and Unknown must not become zero.

The CC BY 4.0 generalized CBS centre [5.5907755595476365,51.43729177688227] lies inside GM1771. Daily Public Domain Mark 1.0 BAG labels Geldrop and Mierlo both lie inside; annual CC BY 4.0 BRT names fourteen settlements. These are identity/reference geometry, not event-time occupancy, isolation, hazard or lifeline state.

The fifteen published neighbourhood populations sum to 40,750, four below the municipality total (-0.010%); deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 40,754. Registered residents omit commuters, hospital patients/staff/visitors, responders and other transient people.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, crisis organisation and care-chain risk
evidenceSources.edition: Final version 1.0 for 2025–2028; regional crisis plan 2024–2027 and care-risk page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The profile treats high river water, extreme rain, dike failure, nature fire, heat, cold/snow/ice, storm and interruption of electricity, gas/heat, data/telecom, drinking water and wastewater treatment as distinct risks and functional chains. It names municipalities, GHOR, water boards, Rijkswaterstaat, Enexis, KPN and Brabant Water as partners; roles do not prove event-time execution or capacity.

The profile is strategic/static and selects no GM1771 Rhine/Meuse/IJssel hydrograph, defence failure, connected inundation footprint or recovery curve. Its public documents provide no operational municipal feed for staffing, warnings, resource commitment or completion.

VRBZO's care-risk profile at https://www.vrbzo.nl/zorgrisicoprofiel/ identifies power, cyber and telecom/ICT failure as leading care-chain risks, recommends regional inflow/throughflow/outflow and patient-evacuation planning, and explicitly reports incomplete insight into dependencies across the care chain.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Official local water, pluvial, heat, nature and mobility evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages and Omgevingsvisie 2040 inspected 3 September 2026; observed event 17–18 June 2020
supports: The official stress test distinguishes an observed 87 mm in five hours on 17–18 June 2020, a 90 mm in one hour 1:500 model scenario and a 160 mm in two hours 1:2,000 model scenario. It says mapped ponding often lasts at most several hours and warns that a dark parcel colour does not prove building entry or toilet/drain failure.

The municipality names Parallelweg, Bisschop van Mierlostraat, Neerakker, Heer Dickbierweg, Beemdstraat, Ori and Luchen storage ponds as local water measures. It says extreme short-duration rain can exceed sewer capacity, nearly 11 km is inspected annually and nearly 16,000 gullies are maintained; these facts do not provide live connectivity, blockage, pump state or capacity.

Water policy at https://www.geldrop-mierlo.nl/waterbeleid and the Omgevingsvisie identify De Dommel and Aa en Maas, Kleine Dommel, Hooidonksebeek, Kleine Beekloop, Goorloop and a Mierlo system not presently connected to Sang/Goorkens. These local/regional mechanisms are not the preset's named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel event.

The heat page https://www.geldrop-mierlo.nl/mogelijke-hittestress says PET depends on radiation, humidity and wind and that the green area between Geldrop and Mierlo is visibly cooler than the built cores. The official Kaartviewer surfaces are public to view, but no documented API/WMS/WFS endpoint, blanket machine-reuse licence, fixed edition or cadence was established; causal ingestion requires owner confirmation.

The mobility page https://www.geldrop-mierlo.nl/mobiliteitbeleid says A67 and A270 plus busy local roads provide access between Eindhoven and Helmond. Static policy and projects are not event-time route passability, emergency throughput or restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap De Dommel / Waterschap Aa en Maas / Het Waterschapshuis / PDOK
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Legal water-system registers and harmonised public water-asset services
evidenceSources.edition: IMWA weekly service and contributor-dependent DAMO snapshot inspected 3 September 2026; De Dommel Legger Waterstaatswerken 2023
supports: The CC BY-SA 4.0 IMWA OGC API is normally refreshed weekly; the CC BY-SA 4.0 water-chain DAMO OGC API at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 has contributor-dependent completeness and update timing. Native identifiers, responsible authority, feature status, registration time, geometry, collection, coverage and NoData must be retained.

The deployed GM1771 polygon query returns 31 sewer-pump, wastewater-treatment, surface-water-pump and weir records, including SVI Mierlo and structures attributed to both De Dommel and Aa en Maas. Sample capacities are partial and units/connectivity are not established in the display; 'gerealiseerd' is register status and never proof of current operation.

The De Dommel 2023 Legger at https://www.dommel.nl/legger and Aa en Maas Legger at https://www.aaenmaas.nl/onswerk/regels/legger/ establish legal location, type and maintenance responsibility for watercourses and structures. They are not live levels, directions, controls, failures, electricity backup, hydraulic capacity or service restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Integration routes for flood, weather, earthquake, water observations and combustible nature
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO 2025.1.6; current public services inspected 3 September 2026
supports: LIWO and https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows expose versioned professional flood scenarios that require specialist interpretation. Causal use must bind an authority-selected event and retain source water body, hydrograph and datum, defence/breach/overtopping/control state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession/dewatering, probability, native resolution, licence, coverage and NoData. LIWO is not a live forecast.

RWS Waterinfo observations are generally produced every ten minutes and are CC0 unless a component says otherwise; the deployed assignment finds zero level and zero discharge stations inside GM1771. Station observations are not continuous hydraulic surfaces or T+72 forecasts, and no local station is NoData rather than zero/safe.

KNMI EDR provides issue/observation/valid-time weather collections, commonly CC BY 4.0, and KNMI FDSN exposes an automatically updated CC BY 4.0 earthquake catalogue. A station/current observation must not be silently extended through T+72 and an event catalogue is not a municipal ground-motion surface.

IPO's Public Domain combustible-nature WFS layer ISOR_RK:isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied at https://servicespub.risicokaart.nl/geoserver/ISOR_RK/wfs?service=WFS&request=GetCapabilities identifies Klein Goor and Molenbos mixed-forest areas attributed to GM1771; metadata was updated 19 February 2026. It proves static eligible geometry, not current fuel/moisture, ignition, plume, access or suppression.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Authoritative road, rail, timetable and event-valid transport context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026; ProRail, OVapi GTFS and NDW services inspected August–September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB geometry is downloadable and exposed through OGC at https://api.pdok.nl/rws/nationaal-wegenbestand-wegen/ogc/v1. The generated GM1771 graph has only two logical A67 series edges to Eindhoven and Someren, both with nominal 260 scenario-unit ceilings and physicalCorridorId NWB-road-67; they are consecutive sections, not independent parallel capacity.

The A67-only graph is a deliberately sparse logical Mobility/Supply transfer graph, not a complete emergency reachability model for the A270/local-road links described by E03, Anna/Helmond access, evacuation, freight or repair. The current engine correctly prevents these unqualified road links from becoming utility topology.

ProRail's CC0 service identifies Geldrop station and the retrieved GTFS feed identifies 44 stop areas, including Sint Annaziekenhuis. Static geometry/timetables do not prove event-time operation, accessibility, passenger capacity or restoration. Deployed NDW current DATEX has zero intersecting GM1771 events; that is partial current NoData, never proof every road remains open through T+72.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM / Anna Zorggroep
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Provider, grid-planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care v1.1 and 2025 activity; provider records dated 2025-09-07 to 2025-12-29; other registers/planning snapshot retrieved 2026
supports: The Public Domain provider WMS/WFS at https://public.geodata.mijnaansluiting.nl/geoserver/mijnaansluiting_open/ows returns Enexis electricity/gas, Brabant Water and Ziggo at the reference point, and no drainage feature. Point/provider territory is responsibility context, not complete coverage, physical topology, live state, quality, capacity or restoration; an empty discipline is Unknown.

The one NBNL sample, postcode 5731XS/service area HMZ Helmond Zuid, reports large-user planning/queue quantities and nineteen projects with earliest year 2026. Capacity/projects are planning snapshots, not open licensed live household load, outage, feeder topology, switching, restoration or T+72 reserve.

The deployment assigns 81 RDI antenna-installation and 20 DUO education records. DUO's machine data at https://onderwijsdata.duo.nl/dataset/c416acd1-e083-4ec6-9203-3b20f98fe143 is normally refreshed daily around 06:15 under CC Attribution; antenna and school registers do not prove coverage/backhaul/power, shelter use, occupancy, stock or opening.

RIVM's CC0 acute-care v1.1 records Anna Zorggroep Geldrop as a 24/7 SEH and acute-obstetrics site with eight treatment rooms and 12,376 reported 2025 visits; the provider page https://www.annaziekenhuis.nl/afdelingen/spoedeisende-hulp/ confirms the regular 24/7 service. Nearby registry points include Elkerliek Helmond 6.16 km, Catharina Eindhoven 8.89 km and Máxima Veldhoven 12.43 km straight-line from the municipal reference point. Static registry/service statements do not establish travel, live beds, staffing, acceptance, backups or cross-boundary incident capacity.

RIVM's 2024 Anna analysis at https://www.rivm.nl/documenten/bereikbaarheidsanalyse-acute-verloskunde-anna-ziekenhuis-geldrop documents a temporary change in acute obstetrics caused by neonatal-nurse availability, illustrating why a static 24/7 registry cannot be treated as every capability's event-time state.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Official first-72-hour preparedness guidance and evidence limits
evidenceSources.edition: Current pages inspected 3 September 2026; national public guidance updated through 2026
supports: The municipality tells residents to prepare for 72 hours without normal services and lists 4–5 litres of water per person, while current national guidance at https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/vraag-en-antwoord/veiligheidsregios-en-crisisbeheersing/wat-zit-er-in-een-noodpakket advises three litres per person per day, or nine litres for 72 hours. The local quantity lacks an explicit per-day qualifier and should not become a hidden stock assumption.

Preparedness advice is not a GM1771 observation of household water, food, cash, batteries, medicines or mutual aid, a guarantee that help arrives at T+72, a distribution plan, or a service-restoration target.

The public pages provide no event-time machine feed, observation time, fixed operational cadence or blanket reuse licence. Preparedness, reception, emergency supply, action execution and recovery must remain measured/confirmed, assumed or Unknown as separate states.

notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1771 pnpm audit:model passes both current tests over ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One complete neighbourhood ordering is reused across eight distinct mechanisms and conflicts with official local rain and heat evidence.
notes: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack and canonical wildfire have the exact same fifteen-neighbourhood order, hash 7bfc64483370: Buitengebied Mierlo, Mierlo-Dorp and Genoenhuis lead; Buitengebied Geldrop-Oost and Neerakkers trail. Earthquake is an all-zero tie; compound differs through saturation.

E03 identifies Neerakker and Luchen among local rain measures and the green area between both cores as cooler. The generic pluvial order puts Neerakkers 15/15 and Luchen 13/15; the heat order puts Buitengebied Mierlo 1/15 and Neerakkers 15/15.

For a controlled fire source [5.59442127407027,51.430280855702414] inside IPO Molenbos and BU17710114, the containing neighbourhood ranks 1/15 with hazard 0.868812; direct source containment passes. The result remains synthetic and lacks event-time fuel, wind, access and suppression calibration.

serviceDependencies.summary: Dependency directions are explainable, but exact eight-service states lack local physical topology, live capacity, backup and restoration calibration.
notes: The trace exposes direct hazard, baseline resilience, upstream dependency, backup and network-transfer stages; for river T+72 the post-network values are power 0.731605, water 0.690927, drainage 0.613696, gas/heating 0.818845, telecom 0.676101, mobility 0.925364, facilities 0.636656 and supply 0.791045.

Provider territories, one NBNL planning sample, 81 antennas, 20 schools, acute-care points, 31 water-register objects and two road edges do not supply physical feeder/pipe/backhaul/catchment topology, live state, pressure/quality, backup endurance, crews, spare capacity or restoration.

The UI correctly states that NWB connectivity is a logical transfer proxy rather than physical utility topology. Exact availability, demand/delivery and reserve values are still synthetic scenario outputs and require adjacent uncertainty/calibration labels.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic contributions reconcile, but most local causes are not linked to authority-selected spatial events, live lifeline evidence or confirmed actions.
notes: The trace distinguishes scenario input, municipality input, regional input and derived model state, and proportional/exact-stage contribution totals reconcile numerically.

River/coastal evidence is only derived screening and the other local hazards are synthetic; unsupportedDimensions is empty. No selected local hydraulic surface, official rain raster, issue-valid weather field, named cyber target, ground-motion field or canonical ignition/spread/plume drives local allocation.

Affected people-equivalent and system pressure are current post-network proxies, while deprived person-hours is cumulative event-attributable weighted local pre-network service shortfall against a matched no-event baseline. Those internal scopes are legitimate but cannot be compared as one observed welfare measure.
Response delay/readiness and intervention effects have no authority, request/confirmation/completion state, resource unit, valid time or local capacity ledger.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent and recovered trajectories are deterministic but not local restoration forecasts, operational plans or commitments.
notes: River forcing persists: severity 0.212721 and internal flood-stress amplitude 0.678268 remain through T+72, with pressure 0.265647, 7,214 affected people-equivalent and 674,831.581125 cumulative local pre-network person-hours. No selected local hydraulic/dewatering event validates this plateau.

Compound T+72 retains severity 0.606471, pressure 0.627933, 28,016 affected people-equivalent and 1,566,856.659612 person-hours; all eight service values are frozen from T+48. Heat remains 23.685071 with drought 0.475565 at T+72; canonical wildfire direct hazard is zero while pressure remains 0.075754. These are exercise dynamics, not observations.

No operator, water board, municipality, care provider or safety-region source supplies GM1771 repair curves, crews/pumps/generators/fuel, emergency water/food/medicine, hospital acceptance, patient transfer or action completion.
T+72 is a dependency checkpoint, not a preparedness guarantee, relief-arrival promise or recovery deadline.

findings.summary: The persistent precise Geldrop-Mierlo major-river impact is unsupported by a selected hydraulically connected event.
findings.evidence: E02 selects no GM1771 Rhine/Meuse/IJssel event; E03 instead identifies Kleine Dommel, Hooidonksebeek, Kleine Beekloop, Goorloop and disconnected Mierlo/Sang-Goorkens mechanisms; E05 offers LIWO event layers but none drives the run. Yet internal flood stress 0.678268 and severity 0.212721 persist through T+72, producing 7,214 affected people-equivalent, 0.265647 post-network pressure and exact eight-service states with unsupportedDimensions=[].
findings.action: Until an authority-selected event is bound, mark direct GM1771 major-river magnitude/impact Unknown and do not present the internal index as metres. For a supported run retain release/event, water body, hydrograph/datum, defence/breach/overtopping/control state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession/dewatering, probability, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData; keep local/regional water and indirect supply mechanisms distinct.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated hazards reuse the same complete fifteen-neighbourhood order and contradict official local mechanism geography.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire all hash to 7bfc64483370, led by Buitengebied Mierlo and ending with Neerakkers. E03 names Neerakker/Luchen water measures and identifies the green inter-core area as cooler; the model ranks Neerakkers 15/15 and Luchen 13/15 for pluvial and Buitengebied Mierlo 1/15 for heat.
findings.action: Replace the common local-risk seed with mechanism-specific, source-dated wind, rainfall/sewer, hydraulic, heat/PET/vulnerability, digital-target, fuel/fire/smoke and access adapters plus explicit coverage/NoData. Add a regression that unrelated nonzero presets cannot share an entire municipal ordering unless a documented common input justifies it.

findings.summary: Official local rainfall scenarios and named interventions do not drive the generic precise pluvial result.
findings.evidence: E03 distinguishes observed 87 mm/5 h, modelled 90 mm/1 h 1:500 and 160 mm/2 h 1:2,000 cases, several-hour ponding and named local measures. The run instead reports T+24 flood stress 0.624955, pressure 0.314790 and 10,036 affected people-equivalent using the common spatial seed. The public Kaartviewer has no established documented machine endpoint, licence, fixed edition or cadence.
findings.action: Obtain owner-confirmed API/export and licence/version, then ingest native surfaces as named model scenarios with duration, depth units, sewer/unpaved assumptions, probability wording, coverage and NoData. Keep the 2020 observation, planning maps, current weather and simulated T+72 states separate; do not use asset geometry causally until connectivity/state/calibration are reviewed.

findings.summary: Exact potable-water, wastewater, drainage and flood-control states lack a connected two-water-board local model.
findings.evidence: E03 assigns surface-water responsibilities to De Dommel and Aa en Maas and drinking water to Brabant Water. E04 returns 31 partial register objects including SVI Mierlo and both boards, but no complete connectivity, flow, live control, electricity backup, pressure/quality or restoration. E07's provider point is responsibility only. River T+72 nevertheless reports water 0.690927 and drainage 0.613696 exactly.
findings.action: Integrate owner-authorized aggregate potable-water, wastewater, sewer, regional drainage and flood-control zones separately, preserving authority, topology class, valid-time state, capacity/backup bands, units, uncertainty and NoData. Keep IMWA/DAMO/provider features non-causal until reviewed mappings exist; use a visibly synthetic fallback where operational data is unavailable or sensitive.

findings.summary: Anna and cross-boundary acute-care continuity are represented as static points rather than an event-time care network.
findings.evidence: E07 records Anna Geldrop as regular 24/7 SEH/acute obstetrics with 8 rooms and 12,376 2025 visits and nearby Elkerliek, Catharina and Máxima sites; its 2024 Anna analysis shows a capability can change with neonatal-nurse availability. E02 says care-chain dependencies and patient inflow/throughflow/outflow/evacuation require regional planning. None supplies live travel, beds, staff, acceptance, backups or supplies, yet facilities availability is exact and falls to 0.636656 in the river run at T+48/T+72.
findings.action: Create an operator/GHOR-authorized aggregate care graph with event-time availability, patient-flow and acceptance states, travel/passability, staff, power/water/telecom/heat backup, fuel, oxygen/medicine/supply, evacuation and uncertainty. Keep registered rooms/annual visits distinct from live incident capacity and protect security-sensitive detail.

findings.summary: Sparse roads, provider territories, planning samples and public registers cannot calibrate exact lifeline topology or restoration.
findings.evidence: E06 supplies two A67 logical series edges, one station, 44 stop areas and zero local current NDW matches; E03 also describes A270/local access. E07 supplies provider responsibility at one point, one NBNL planning sample, 81 antenna and 20 education records. None establishes event-time route/rail status, physical electricity/gas/water/telecom networks, coverage/backhaul, supply routing, facility operation, repair resources or capacity.
findings.action: Keep source roles explicit: NWB/ProRail/GTFS geometry/schedule, NDW issue-valid partial events, provider polygons responsibility, NBNL planning, and RDI/DUO/RIVM registrations. Use operator/authority-approved aggregate zones and restoration bands where available; otherwise publish versioned synthetic assumptions with uncertainty and never infer sensitive topology.

findings.summary: The first-72-hour trajectory has no auditable local intervention, authority, resource or completion ledger.
findings.evidence: E02 assigns distinct partner and GHOR responsibilities; E08 is household preparedness guidance rather than measured readiness and contains a water-quantity ambiguity relative to national advice. The model emits exact response/recovery, reserve and cumulative burden without warning, evacuation/shelter, hospital flow, emergency-water, food/medicine, traffic, pump, generator/fuel or repair actions/resources.
findings.action: Represent each intervention with authority, target/units, trigger, proposed/requested/confirmed/started/completed/failed/cancelled state, issue/valid/expiry time, crews, vehicles, pumps, generators, fuel, stocks, dependencies, confidence and source. residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning-model audit, not a KNMI, Rijkswaterstaat, WMCN, De Dommel, Aa en Maas, VRBZO, Geldrop-Mierlo municipality, Anna or operator forecast, warning, probability, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration commitment.

Generalized CBS neighbourhoods and BAG/BRT labels are overview aggregation, not parcels, catchments, flood compartments, sewers, water-control systems, heat/PET surfaces, woodland fuel, incident perimeters, utility topology, hospital occupancy or emergency routes.

No selected Rhine/Meuse/IJssel boundary condition, defence state, breach/overtopping case, connected inundation footprint, depth/velocity, arrival/recession, probability or NoData mask drives GM1771. Internal flood stress is not metres.

Official municipal rainfall maps are observations/model scenarios with separate durations and probabilities; their viewer lacks an established documented machine endpoint, licence, fixed version and cadence. They cannot silently become observations, forecasts or causal surfaces.

HWH records and water-board Leggers are legal/register geometry rather than connected, live hydraulic state. 'Gerealiseerd' does not prove operation; partial capacities and missing units/records remain Unknown.

NWB, ProRail and GTFS are static geometry/schedule context. The Mobility/Supply-only restriction is correct, but the two-edge A67 graph is not complete A270/local-road/rail/hospital-access, evacuation, freight or repair state; nominal ceilings are not throughput.

No complete safe public source supplies Enexis electricity/gas topology, Brabant Water pipes/pressure/quality, municipal sewer connectivity, water-board live controls, Ziggo/other telecom backhaul, facility dependencies, supplies, backups, crews or restoration. Sensitive detail was not inferred.

NBNL capacity is planning rather than live load/outage; provider polygons are responsibility rather than topology; RDI antennas are not coverage/backhaul/state; DUO/RIVM points are not shelters, live hospital capacity or supplies.
The controlled Molenbos source is synthetic and tests containment only. IPO eligibility does not describe future ignition, fuel/moisture, flame/spread, smoke, access, suppression or recovery.

Cyber lacks a named target/architecture/attack path; earthquake needs a selected event and ground-motion surface; heat/winter/storm need issue-valid KNMI forcing; North-Sea coastal surge is not a substitute for local/regional water.

Registered residents omit patients/staff/visitors, commuters and responders. Household readiness, emergency-support/reception/water points, stocks, staff, vehicles and repair priorities remain assumed or Unknown; official 72-hour advice is not measured stock or a deadline.

Affected people-equivalent and system pressure are current post-network proxies; deprived person-hours is cumulative event-attributable weighted local pre-network shortfall against a matched no-event baseline. Neither is identified customers, casualties, displacement, welfare loss or economic damage, and six-hour checkpoints can miss fast fire, rain, traffic and control changes.
